parameter.name: blob
parameter.description: The blob name, including any virtual directory prefix.

parameter.name: readConcurrency
parameter.description: Ranged GETs in flight at once, default 4. These threads wait on the network rather than on a core, so the count is not tied to CPUs and the upper bound of 256 is a typo guard, not a ration. readBlockSize x readConcurrency is held in heap per transfer: above a quarter of the heap the operator logs what it is holding, and only a figure at or above the whole heap is refused, because that cannot run.

parameter.name: readBlockSize
parameter.description: Bytes per ranged GET, e.g. 32MB. Default 8MB. On a far-region account this matters more than readConcurrency: throughput there is dominated by per-request cost, so fewer larger requests beats more parallel ones and costs no extra threads. Above 4MB Azure will not compute a per-range MD5, so range verification switches off and says so in the log. Held memory is readBlockSize x readConcurrency.

parameter.name: verifyBlocks
parameter.description: false to skip per-range MD5 verification. Only has effect when readBlockSize is 4MB or less, which is the largest range Azure will hash.

parameter.name: readTimeout
parameter.description: Per-range liveness bound, e.g. 300s or 5m. Unset, it is derived from the range size against a floor rate. Set it where the link and the distance to the storage account are known: the derived floor was chosen against throughput measured in one environment, and a constant that fits a lab does not fit every deployment. It bounds a dead connection, not a slow one.
